A's two neighbors are linked, so A scores 1.00, down to F at 0; the pendant G has a single neighbor, so its value is undefined, drawn faded and listed as None." width="100%"} The local clustering coefficient measures how close a node's neighbors are to being a complete subgraph (clique). For a node with k neighbors, it's the fraction of possible edges between neighbors that actually exist. For undirected graphs: `C(v) = 2 * triangles(v) / (k * (k-1))` For directed graphs, edgecase uses Fagiolo's (2007) definition, as `networkx.clustering()` does. Two neighbors of `v` that are linked close a triangle whichever way its three arcs point, so all four kinds of directed triangle count: `C(v) = T(v) / (k_tot * (k_tot - 1) - 2 * k_recip)`, where `T(v)` is the number of directed triangles through `v`, `k_tot` is its in-degree plus out-degree, and `k_recip` is the number of neighbors it links to in both directions. Values lie in `[0, 1]`. Degrees count distinct neighbors other than the node itself, so parallel edges and self-loops are ignored. Nodes with fewer than 2 neighbors return `None` (clustering undefined). Time complexity: `O(m * d_max)` where `m` is edges and `d_max` is maximum degree. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store clustering coefficient values. If `None`, uses `local_clustering_coefficient` as the attribute name. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary mapping node IDs to clustering coefficients. If `False`, stores values as node attributes and returns the Graph for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, Optional[float]], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True` we receive a dictionary mapping node IDs to clustering coefficients (`0.0` to `1.0`), or `None` for nodes with degree < `2`. If `return_dict=` is `False`, this returns self for method chaining. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~clustering_coefficient`) : The same values, with 0 instead of None for low degree. [](`~average_clustering_coefficient`) : The mean over all nodes. [](`~transitivity`) : The fraction of closed triples in the whole graph. [](`~random_reference`) : A random graph with the same degrees, to compare against. ## Examples {.doc-examples} `A` has four neighbors, so six pairs of them could be linked, and only `B`-`C` is: its clustering is 1/6. `B` and `C` score 1, since their two neighbors are linked. `D` and `E` have one neighbor each, so their clustering is undefined: ::: {#7854aea6 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges( [("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("A", "D"), ("A", "E")] ) graph.local_clustering_coefficient() graph.get_node_df().select("label", "local_clustering_coefficient") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: With `return_dict=True`, nothing is stored and the values come back keyed by node ID, with `None` for the undefined ones: ::: {#ccf3da8a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.local_clustering_coefficient(return_dict=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {3: 1.0, 1: 0.16666666666666666, 5: None, 4: None, 2: 1.0} ``` ::: ::: ### Friends of friends `karate_club()` links the 34 members of a university karate club who met outside the club, before it split in two. The members with the most friends have the least clustered circles: only 15 of the 136 pairs of the administrator's 17 friends are friends themselves, and 18 of the 120 pairs of the instructor's 16: ::: {#ecd58c07 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate = ec.karate_club().local_clustering_coefficient() ( karate.get_node_df() .sort("degree", descending=True) .select("label", "role", "degree", "local_clustering_coefficient") .head(5) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

Member `11`, with a single friend, has no value and is drawn gray: ::: {#0ac72a0f .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate.layout_kamada_kawai().plot( layout="pos", color_by="local_clustering_coefficient", size_by="degree", label_by="label", ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### More than chance? `random_reference()` rewires the club into a random graph where every member keeps the same number of friends. Its triangles mostly fall apart, and the average clustering drops from 0.57 to 0.29: ::: {#7f9d4e1a .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} reference = karate.random_reference(seed=1).local_clustering_coefficient() ( karate.average_clustering_coefficient(), reference.average_clustering_coefficient(), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` (0.5706384782076823, 0.28969976582433327) ``` ::: ::: The leaders score a little higher in the reference (right), 0.18 for the instructor and 0.20 for the administrator, so what the club has beyond chance is the tight groups at its edges: ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#68d5f9cb .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate.plot( layout="pos", color_by="local_clustering_coefficient", size_by="degree", label_by="label", width=320, height=360, legend=False, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}
